messages.author: a117157461b73acc
messages.subject: How are CFI and TLI nd RMSEA and SRMR  calculated in lavaan?
parts: I wonder how CFI and TLI  and SRMR    and "rmsea.ci.lower", "rmsea.ci.upper" are calculated in lavaan. What formula could I use to calculate such values manually and yield same results as that output by lavaan?

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: How are CFI and TLI nd RMSEA and SRMR calculated in lavaan?
parts:
The cool thing about open source code (like lavaan) is that if you want to know how something is done, you don't need to take anyone's word for it, you can go and look.

The file to look at is:
https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/d7a6ea7ed5c1b21e3e5f7a909d78788579f300f7/R/lav_fit_measures.R

And the gist of the code for the lower CI of RMSEA is (pulling out all of the error checking and stuff):
lower.lambda <- function(lambda) { 
  pchisq(X2, df=df, ncp=lambda) - 0.95
 }
lambda.l <- try(uniroot(f=lower.lambda, lower=0, upper=X2)$root, silent=TRUE)
GG <- 0
["rmsea.ci.lower"] <- ( lambda.l/((N-GG)*df) ) * sqrt(G)

(Where G is the number of groups, usually 1).

And here's CFI:

t1 <- max( c(X2 - df, 0) )
                t2 <- max( c(X2 - df, X2.null - df.null, 0) )
                if(isTRUE(all.equal(t1,0)) &&
                   isTRUE(all.equal(t2,0))) {
                    indices["cfi"] <- 1
                } else {
                    indices["cfi"] <- 1 - t1/t2
                }

messages.subject: Re: How are CFI and TLI nd RMSEA and SRMR calculated in lavaan?
parts:
I'm not sure what you're trying to do.

If you want the measures, you can  use the fitMeasures() function to extract them from the fitted model. 

 fit <- sem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy)
fitMeasures(fit)

If you want to calculate them by hand, what information do you want to calculate them from?

If you have X2 = fitted model chi-square, X2.null is null model chi square, df is fitted df, and df.null is null df, then:

t1 <- max( c(X2 - df, 0) )
t2 <- max( c(X2 - df, X2.null - df.null, 0) )
cfi  <- 1 - t1/t2

But you get all those statistics you want using the fitMeasures function, and you can also use that to get CFI.

If you copy and paste my email, which includes explanations, it won't run. :)

If you want to calculate them 'by hand' you're probably better of with a book or article that gives the formulas, your favorite internet search engine can probably help you out. E.g. I typed <rmsea lower confidence interval equation> into my favorite search engine, and found this article: https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10062422 (by, amongst others, the author of Lavaan) which contains the formulas. 

Hope that helps,

Jeremy

‫في الخميس، 10 ديسمبر 2020 في 1:48 ص تمت كتابة ما يلي بواسطة ‪Jeremy Miles‬‏ <‪jeremy...@gmail.com‬‏>:‬

I'm not sure what you're trying to do.

If you want the measures, you can  use the fitMeasures() function to extract them from the fitted model. 

 fit <- sem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy)
fitMeasures(fit)

If you want to calculate them by hand, what information do you want to calculate them from?

If you have X2 = fitted model chi-square, X2.null is null model chi square, df is fitted df, and df.null is null df, then:

t1 <- max( c(X2 - df, 0) )
t2 <- max( c(X2 - df, X2.null - df.null, 0) )
cfi  <- 1 - t1/t2

But you get all those statistics you want using the fitMeasures function, and you can also use that to get CFI.

If you copy and paste my email, which includes explanations, it won't run. :)

If you want to calculate them 'by hand' you're probably better of with a book or article that gives the formulas, your favorite internet search engine can probably help you out. E.g. I typed <rmsea lower confidence interval equation> into my favorite search engine, and found this article: https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10062422 (by, amongst others, the author of Lavaan) which contains the formulas. 

Hope that helps,

Jeremy

في الأربعاء، 9 ديسمبر 2020 في تمام الساعة 9:21:49 م UTC+3، كتب jeremy...@gmail.com رسالة نصها:
The cool thing about open source code (like lavaan) is that if you want to know how something is done, you don't need to take anyone's word for it, you can go and look.

The file to look at is:
https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/d7a6ea7ed5c1b21e3e5f7a909d78788579f300f7/R/lav_fit_measures.R

And the gist of the code for the lower CI of RMSEA is (pulling out all of the error checking and stuff):
lower.lambda <- function(lambda) { 
  pchisq(X2, df=df, ncp=lambda) - 0.95
 }
lambda.l <- try(uniroot(f=lower.lambda, lower=0, upper=X2)$root, silent=TRUE)
GG <- 0
["rmsea.ci.lower"] <- ( lambda.l/((N-GG)*df) ) * sqrt(G)

(Where G is the number of groups, usually 1).

And here's CFI:

t1 <- max( c(X2 - df, 0) )
                t2 <- max( c(X2 - df, X2.null - df.null, 0) )
                if(isTRUE(all.equal(t1,0)) &&
                   isTRUE(all.equal(t2,0))) {
                    indices["cfi"] <- 1
                } else {
                    indices["cfi"] <- 1 - t1/t2
                }
